indications: Short-term treatment of insomnia — difficulty with sleep onset and maintenance

dosage.adult: IR: 5 mg (women) or 5–10 mg (men) immediately before bed. CR: 6.25–12.5 mg
dosage.renal_adjustment: No significant adjustment

warnings: FDA black box warning (2019): complex sleep behaviors including sleep-driving have resulted in deaths — contraindicate in patients who have experienced this
Lower dose recommended for women — slower clearance
Rebound insomnia on discontinuation
contraindications: History of complex sleep behaviors with zolpidem or other sedatives
interactions: Alcohol — dramatically increases complex sleep behavior risk
counseling_points: Take immediately before bed — only when you have 7–8 hours available
Women should take lower dose — 5 mg
Do not take with alcohol — can cause sleep-driving or other dangerous behaviors
Short-term use only — no more than 4 weeks
Schedule IV — refills permitted in NYS
pearls: Federal Schedule IV and NYS Schedule IV
FDA required dose reduction recommendation for women in 2013 — women clear zolpidem 50% slower than men
Complex sleep behaviors (sleep-driving, sleep-eating, sleep-sex) are idiosyncratic and unpredictable — FDA added black box warning in 2019
Z-drugs (zolpidem, zaleplon, eszopiclone) were originally thought to have lower abuse potential than benzodiazepines — now known to have similar addiction risk
